An 87-year-old male is hospitalized due to an acute diverticular bleed and receives intravenous fluid
resuscitation along with 2 units of packed red blood cells. A CT scan of the abdomen reveals
diverticulosis at the splenic flexure. On the third day of hospitalization, he experiences another bloody
bowel movement, but his hemoglobin levels and symptoms remain stable. Physical examination
reveals swelling, erythema, and warmth in the right leg, along with pain upon passive dorsiflexion of the
right foot. His vital signs include a temperature of 37.3 °C (99.1 °F), blood pressure of 132/78 mmHg,
pulse of 92/min, respiratory rate of 12/min, and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Ultrasound
findings indicate a non-compressible right popliteal vein. Laboratory results are as follows. What is the
next best step in management? | **Laboratory value** | **Result** | | --- | --- | | Leukocyte count |
9000/mm3 | | Hemoglobin | 7.2 g/dL | | Platelet count | 160,000/mm3 | | INR | 1.0 | | D-dimer | 1500
ng/mL | Answer Choices: (A) Warfarin initiation without bridging therapy (B) Unfractionated heparin (C)
Compression stockings only (D) Cefazolin (E) Thrombolysis (F) Surgical thrombectomy (G) Inferior
vena cava filter placement (H) Low molecular weight heparin (I) Observation with vital signs monitoring
(J) Direct oral anticoagulant
 A. Unfractionated heparin

B. Warfarin initiation without bridging therapy
C. Compression stockings only
D. Observation with vital signs monitoring
E. Low molecular weight heparin
F. Cefazolin
G. Surgical thrombectomy
H. Inferior vena cava filter placement
I. Thrombolysis
